Rules / Maintainability

SK7101 A non-public member has no documentation comment

A declaration that is not publicly visible through its whole containing chain, and carries no documentation comment. Disabled by default; enable it per path.

CategoryMaintainability
Default severitynone
ScopeSyntax
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseyes
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since1.3

Why

SK7010 is this rule over the public surface, and the two are meant to partition one population: the same predicates decide what a documentable declaration is, and the only difference is which side of the accessibility line it falls on. What is different is the volume. This is the highest-firing uncovered inspection in the whole parity measurement — 3 408 findings — and SK7010, which already ships, produces 1 868 on Testing/corpus at warning. So it ships disabled: defaultSeverity: none, the same as SK7010, turned on per path by a repository that wants it for the code where internal documentation earns its keep. That is a decision about a report, not about a rule: a finding nobody can see past is not a finding.

Example

Instead of:

sealed class Archetype {
    internal int Count { get; }
}

Write:

sealed class Archetype {
    /// <summary>How many entities the archetype holds.</summary>
    internal int Count { get; }
}

When it does not fire

⚠ Disabled by default, so it produces nothing until a repository asks for it, and that is the whole disposal of its noise. docs/plan/17 names this the clearest case in the parity map for not letting a fire count drive a decision, and the count is why it ships at none rather than why it ships loud. Turning it on repository-wide on a codebase that has never documented an internal is the failure docs/plan/16 § R3 describes; the intended use is a scoped .editorconfig section over the paths where it means something. ⚠ Its predicates are `SK7010`'s, unchanged, with the accessibility test negated, and that is deliberate rather than convenient: the two rules are meant to partition one population, so a declaration cannot be reported by both or missed by both because they disagree about what is documentable. It therefore inherits every one of SK7010's exclusions — accessors, explicit interface implementations, operators, finalizers, record positional members and generated code are not reported, an <inheritdoc/> counts as documentation, and an empty /// does not. ⚠ Fields are excluded, and for a non-public rule that is the largest single exclusion there is. Private fields outnumber every other kind of non-public member and a count field's name is its documentation; including them is how the rule would become unusable even for the repositories that want it. ⚠ An `override` is reported, for the same reason SK7010 reports one: this rule asks whether the declaration is documented, and SK7100 is the rule that says what to write there. ⚠ Because it is disabled by default, Roslyn does not run this analyzer at all in a repository that has not enabled it — which is why it is a separate analyzer rather than a branch of the metrics pass, where the predicate would run on every member of every compilation.

Configuration

  • dotnet_diagnostic.SK7101.severity (none by default; set it per path to enable)
